one_liner: Safe-Rust fork of the image-rs gif crate whose census-routed k-means quantizer claims faster GIF encode than FFmpeg palettegen/paletteuse.
what_it_does: rusty_gif is gif 0.14.2 with color_quant 1.1.0's NeuQuant vendored in, renamed, and used as the GIF codec of the rff ffmpeg-style CLI. The API is the gif crate's: DecodeOptions/Decoder and a low-level StreamingDecoder for reading, Encoder for writing, and Frame::from_rgb*/from_rgba* for turning true-colour pixels into an indexed frame. The only functional change against upstream is inside Frame::from_rgb*/from_rgba*, which now picks a quantizer per frame; replacing an FFmpeg palettegen/paletteuse graph means calling Frame::from_rgb then Encoder::write_frame, or going through rff.
how_it_is_fast: Palette building is priced by colour diversity, not pixel count: a HashMap census of unique RGBA colours routes each frame to an exact palette (256 or fewer colours), to median-cut initialisation plus frequency-weighted k-means (Lloyd iterations over the unique colours, 3/2/1 iterations at up to 32,768/49,152/65,536 colours, brute-force nearest of 256 centres), or, above 65,536 colours, to NeuQuant with samplefac = ceil(pixels / 125,000) clamped to [speed, 30] (17 at 1080p). Pixel-to-index mapping is memoised per unique colour instead of searched per pixel, and NeuQuant's contest() loop is split so its decay loop auto-vectorises. LZW is the unmodified weezl crate and the decoder is upstream's, so nothing on the decode side explains the 'up to 2.5x faster decode' line.
when_to_use: Rust code already on the gif crate whose time goes into Frame::from_rgb/from_rgba NeuQuant training, especially high-resolution frames with at most 65,536 unique colours (screenshots, UI captures, flat graphics, cartoons), where the census route avoids per-pixel training.
You want MSE/PSNR-optimal palettes without dithering: weighted k-means minimises exactly the frequency-weighted squared error PSNR measures.
You need a pure-Rust, #![forbid(unsafe_code)] GIF encoder and decoder with no C toolchain, and can accept a young single-maintainer fork.
Per-frame encoding of independent stills where the current path is an FFmpeg palettegen + paletteuse filter graph run once per image.
when_not_to_use: You want dithered or perceptually tuned output: there is no dithering on any route, and the only quality gate is PSNR against FFmpeg with dither=none (FFmpeg's default is sierra2_4a).

You rely on the speed argument: the k-means route ignores it and the high-diversity route overrides it (samplefac 17 at 1080p), so from_rgb no longer means NeuQuant at full quality; set RUSTY_GIF_Q_POLICY=upstream for byte-identical pre-fork output.

Animations that need one stream-wide palette or frame-difference cropping: Frame::from_rgb* builds an independent palette per frame, while palettegen's default stats_mode=full builds one palette for the whole stream.
Decode speed is the goal: the decoder is unchanged gif 0.14.2 code and the decode claim has no table or workload.

You need a tested, fuzzed codec: the fork carries none of upstream's tests/, fuzz/, gif-afl/ or benches/ directories, only unit tests in src/, and it is one code commit (2026-08-12) plus README and allocator-pin edits.

integration.dependencies: weezl 0.1.10 (pure-Rust LZW); dev-dependency rusty_alloc-api =1.1.6 used as the examples' global allocator
integration.platforms: any std target; no SIMD intrinsics (relies on auto-vectorisation); the crate root is #![cfg(feature = "std")], so a no_std build compiles to an empty crate; CI runs ubuntu, windows and macos latest
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the quantizer keeps no global state but reads RUSTY_GIF_Q_POLICY and RUSTY_GIF_TRACE from the environment on every frame
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — not a drop-in for FFmpeg (it is a library, or the rff CLI); for gif-crate users it is the gif 0.14.2 API under a new crate name, but Frame::from_rgb*/from_rgba* produce different palettes and bytes

gotchas: A library that panics on its environment: an unrecognised RUSTY_GIF_Q_POLICY value panics at encode time, and the variable is read per frame.

Transparency gets no reserved palette slot: the single transparent colour is clustered as an RGBA point (alpha is a fourth k-means channel) and its cluster's index becomes the transparent index, so any opaque colours sharing that cluster would come out transparent; every quantizer test uses opaque pixels only (from reading quantize.rs and kmeans.rs, not run).

examples/stage_profile.rs rebuilds the pre-fork path (NeuQuant speed 1 on every pixel) and asserts byte equality with Frame::from_rgb, so under the default policy it panics on any frame with more than 256 colours unless RUSTY_GIF_Q_POLICY=upstream; examples/encode_bench.rs times rusty_gif alone (best-of-N wall time under rusty_alloc) and has no FFmpeg arm.
quantize.rs's module docs and Policy comment still describe the frequency-capped UniqueStream NeuQuant route as the default; the shipped Auto policy never selects it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The GIF siblings are C: msf_gif (single-header SSE encoder benchmarked against gif.h and jo_gif) for raw encode throughput in C/C++, and gif_load, giflib-turbo and AnimatedGIF as decoders. Pick rusty_gif only when you need a pure safe-Rust encoder with PSNR-oriented palettes; it has no measured decode edge over any of them.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: single-frame encode of 8 unpublished frames (CIF to 1080p), rusty_gif's auto quantizer against FFmpeg 8.1.2 palettegen + paletteuse dither=none, 0.40-0.67x of FFmpeg's CPU time with +0.20 to +4.07 dB PSNR and 15/15 paired wins per frame. CPU, OS, rustc version and flags, the FFmpeg build and command line, and whether palettegen's default reserve_transparent (255-colour palette) was turned off are not stated, and the two arms do different quantization work.
measurement_notes: Beyond the verifier's caveats: remade_ffmpeg_rs now has two public timing harnesses, tools/bench/codec-bench.ps1 (added 2026-09-06) and tools/bench/pinab.py (added 2026-09-10, the 'pinned, High priority, ABBA-interleaved' harness), but both postdate rusty_gif's numbers, which appear in the repo's only code commit on 2026-08-12, so neither is the harness that produced them. The monorepo copy (remade_ffmpeg_rs crates/rusty_gif) holds the same two examples and no bench notes, so the 'repo bench notes' that UPSTREAM-CHANGES.md cites are not public in either repository. Neither fits this comparison as published: pinab.py takes each arm's self-reported 'total <ms> ms' line (FFmpeg prints no such line, so the FFmpeg arm needs a PINAB_DUR regex that is not published), and codec-bench.ps1 is a decode harness that checks work parity against ffprobe frame counts. codec-bench.ps1's own header says the project's earlier Windows CPU-time readings (TotalProcessorTime) were multiples of 15.625 ms and produced published differences that were two ticks; the rusty_gif README reports 'pinned CPU time', and a single CIF frame encodes in milliseconds, so if that clock was used the smaller frames sit near its resolution. That is a plausible flaw, not a demonstrated one. No correctness bug was found behind the numbers: the k-means and memoised-mapping changes are deterministic, the upstream policy is kept as a byte-identical oracle, and the examples' asserts are consistent with that. Tier C stands.
status_note: Active only in the sense of README edits: one code commit (2026-08-12), two rusty_alloc-api pin bumps, then three 'docs: N active installs' commits whose banner (874) is the crates.io download count; MIT OR Apache-2.0 and small enough to vendor, 1 star, two open bot-style PRs (rusty_alloc-api =2.2.0, release-plz).
